You are adding a SHADOW observation-verifier hook to freytag-forge (Python 3.12). Working directory: /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge. export PYTHONPATH=/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge TMPDIR=/tmp CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_URL=https://w.example; run `.venv/bin/python`. No network, no live model call, no uv. Do not git commit. NEVER print or write any credential. NO regular expressions. No story vocabulary (no Kristin, truck, laptop, drawer, Michelle) in non-test code. YOU MAY EDIT ONLY: storygame/runtime/capture.py and a new tests/test_observation_shadow.py. If an existing test elsewhere pins the exact keys of the after_commit record it should still pass because the new key is only added when a verifier is set; you may not edit other files. Read first: storygame/runtime/capture.py (WorldCapture.after_commit, before_turn), storygame/runtime/observation_verifier.py (ObservationVerifier, relations_from_context, VerifierReport, QUESTION_VERSION; already built and tested, do not change it), storygame/runtime/item_facts.py (ItemFactsProvider._observation_context, observation_request), tests/test_runtime_capture.py and tests/test_observation_mode.py for fixture style.

BUILD: `WorldCapture` gets a public attribute `shadow_verifier: ObservationVerifier | None = None` (set in __init__; the constructor signature does not change; nothing in web_demo, engine or configuration sets it, so the product default is OFF). In `after_commit`, BEFORE `apply_item_facts` runs (the world must be the one the narrator saw), if `self.shadow_verifier` is set AND `self.provider.observation_request` is not None AND `self.provider._observation_context()` returns a context, call `self.shadow_verifier.begin_turn()` then `verify(narration, relations_from_context(context))` and add ONE key `observation_shadow` to the returned record (and to `self.last_after`, which is the same dict): {'outcome': report.outcome, 'requests': report.requests, 'elapsed_s': report.elapsed_s, 'failure': report.failure, 'question_version': QUESTION_VERSION, 'accepted': report.accepted, 'verdicts': [{'thing': v.relation.thing, 'verdict': v.verdict, 'score': v.score}, ...]}. Use the module's existing JSON helper if the record is passed through it. The record has NO `observation_shadow` key when the verifier is unset, the request is None, or the context is None (so every existing record is byte-identical). ANY exception inside the shadow step, including ObservationScopeTooLarge, is swallowed and recorded as {'outcome': 'shadow_error', 'requests': 0, 'elapsed_s': 0.0, 'failure': <exception class name only>, 'question_version': QUESTION_VERSION, 'accepted': False, 'verdicts': []}; it never changes `raw`, `issues`, the provider, the world, the narration or any other record field, and it never raises. The verifier is shadow only: its verdict must not influence anything.

TESTS FIRST in tests/test_observation_shadow.py (hermetic, fake ask returning noul scores, real ObservationVerifier, real provider fixtures in the style of tests/test_observation_mode.py): off by default (no key, ask never called); with a verifier and an observation request the record carries the key with the verdicts and exactly one ask call whose state holds the narration; a rejecting verdict changes nothing else (record fields other than the new key equal a run without the verifier; world facts identical); ask returning None -> outcome 'unavailable' recorded, turn unchanged; ask raising -> swallowed (verifier already guards it) and a monkeypatched verifier that raises -> 'shadow_error' with the class name; no observation request -> no key and no ask call; the narration text never appears in the recorded failure. Keep the file focused.

FINISH: ruff check and ruff format your files; report pass counts and quote the final shadow step.

tasks.spec: You are making one tiny additive change to the Jev client in freytag-forge (Python 3.12). Working directory: /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge. export PYTHONPATH=/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge TMPDIR=/tmp CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_URL=https://w.example; run `.venv/bin/python`. No network, no live model call, no uv. Do not git commit. NEVER print or write any credential. NO regular expressions. No story vocabulary (no Kristin, truck, laptop, drawer, Michelle) in non-test code. YOU MAY EDIT ONLY: storygame/runtime/jev.py and tests/test_runtime_jev.py (add tests; change no existing assertion). Read both first. The Worker's /jev response body has the shape {'answers': {...}, 'model': '<model name and version>', 'trace_id': '...'}; today `JevClient.ask` throws the model name away, so a calibration run cannot record which Jev version answered. BUILD: `JevClient.last_model: str | None` (set to None in __init__ and at the start of every `ask`; set to the body's 'model' only when it is a non-empty string and the answers were valid, otherwise None), and `JevClient.last_status: int | None` (None at the start of every ask; the HTTP status of the last response when one was received, kept for the HTTPError case too via its .code). `ask` return values, request_count and every existing behaviour stay exactly the same, including returning None on every failure. TESTS FIRST: success sets last_model from the body and last_status 200; a body without a model leaves None; an error body (status 'error') leaves last_model None; an HTTPError with code 429 sets last_status 429 and returns None; the next successful ask resets the previous failure's status; existing tests unchanged. FINISH: ruff check and format both files; report pass counts.

tasks.spec:
You are building the calibration harness for the observation verifier in freytag-forge (Python 3.12), in the style of scripts/ringer/environment_narration/jev_boarding_probe.py (offline-first; billed only with explicit --confirm and caps). Working directory: /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge. export PYTHONPATH=/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge TMPDIR=/tmp CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_URL=https://w.example; run `.venv/bin/python`. No network, no live model call, no uv. Do not git commit. NEVER print or write any credential. NO regular expressions. No story vocabulary (no Kristin, truck, laptop, drawer, Michelle) in non-test code. YOU MAY EDIT ONLY: new scripts/ringer/environment_narration/verifier_calibration.py and new tests/test_verifier_calibration.py. Read first: scripts/ringer/environment_narration/jev_boarding_probe.py and tests/test_jev_boarding_probe.py (CLI, redaction, row-writing, test style), storygame/runtime/observation_verifier.py (ObservationVerifier, Relation, QUESTION_VERSION, VerifierReport; do not change it), storygame/runtime/jev.py (JevClient; a sibling task is adding `last_model` and `last_status` attributes, so read them with getattr(client, 'last_model', None)), and the corpus files scripts/ringer/environment_narration/verifier_corpus/cases-*.jsonl (JSONL, fields id, story, category, narration, relations[{thing,place,holder,label}], undetectable_invention, note; labels 'accept'/'reject'). Do NOT run a billed call; tests use a fake client only.

MODES (argparse):
1. `--validate-corpus [--lock]`: load every cases-*.jsonl; check fields/types, unique ids across files, labels, exactly one of place/holder or both null, category in the ten known ones (positive_plain, positive_paraphrase, negated, hypothetical_or_remembered, wrong_holder, wrong_place, not_mentioned, lookalike_substitute, invention_unreported, multi_mixed), at least 200 cases, relation reject share 45-55%, `undetectable_invention` true exactly for invention_unreported. Print counts by category, story and label plus the per-file and combined SHA-256. Exit 1 with every failing id printed on any problem. With --lock write scripts/ringer/environment_narration/verifier_corpus/corpus.lock.json ({'files': {name: sha256}, 'combined': sha256, 'cases': n, 'relations': n}). The lock freezes the labels: --run refuses unless the lock exists and matches the current files.
2. default dry run (no flag, or --dry-run): print cases, relations, planned requests (= cases x --samples, default 2; one request per case, all of the case's relations batched), a token estimate (characters of the JSON-encoded request / 4), and a USD ceiling at 0.042 USD per million input tokens times 1.5. No network, no credentials read.
3. `--run --confirm --max-calls N --max-usd X --out rows.json`: refuse without --confirm, if planned requests > --max-calls, if the ceiling > --max-usd, or without a matching lock. Build `JevClient.from_environment()` and one fresh `ObservationVerifier(client.ask)` per request (call begin_turn). Order: deterministic shuffle with a fixed seed, samples interleaved. Write the rows file after EVERY call. Row fields: call_index, case_id, sample, story, category, undetectable_invention, narration_chars, relations [{thing, label, verdict, score}], outcome, failure, latency_ms, jev_model (getattr last_model), thresholds (accept_above, reject_below), question_version, corpus_combined_hash. Stop (and record stop_reason) after 3 consecutive outcomes in {unavailable, malformed}, on last_status 429 or >=500, or at --max-calls. Redact the Worker token from everything written. Never print the narration of a case to stdout during a run.
4. `--report --rows rows.json --out report.md`: render EVERY row's result (case id, category, labels vs verdicts, scores) plus these tables, each by category, by story, by jev_model and overall: relation counts; FALSE ACCEPTS (label reject, verdict accept) with a list of each; FALSE REJECTS (label accept, verdict reject); UNCERTAIN and UNAVAILABLE counts split by label; the strict accept-label failure rate (uncertain or unavailable or reject on an accept label, because the product would fail closed); sample-to-sample disagreement rate for the same case; latency p50/p95; the Wilson 95% upper bound of the false-accept rate over the reject-labelled relations, with a sentence that the sample is limited. GATE section: 'zero observed false accepts on required relations' and 'false rejects at most 5% of accept-labelled relations' (state both the plain false-reject rate and the strict rate), each PASS/FAIL, with the sentence 'The gate is evaluated at the thresholds recorded in the rows.' The invention_unreported cases are reported in their own section, NOT in the gate, with the sentence 'Unreported inventions are not detected by this verifier; these rows only confirm the required relation.' Add a clearly labelled POST-HOC threshold sweep (accept_above in 0.5,0.6,0.65,0.7,0.8,0.9; reject_below = 1 - accept_above, recomputed from stored scores) marked 'not the gate; do not tune and re-score on the same corpus'.

TESTS FIRST in tests/test_verifier_calibration.py (hermetic; use tmp_path corpora and a fake client; import the script as a module in the way tests/test_jev_boarding_probe.py does): validation accepts a good tiny corpus (monkeypatch the 200-case minimum through a module constant) and rejects each broken rule; lock write and mismatch refusal; dry run makes no client and prints the counts; --run refuses without --confirm / over --max-calls / over --max-usd / without lock; a fake run writes rows after each call and stops after 3 consecutive unavailable; report arithmetic on a hand-built rows file with known false accepts, false rejects, uncertain and unavailable (assert the exact counts and the gate PASS/FAIL lines) and the invention section outside the gate; the token never appears in outputs. Keep the file focused.

FINISH: ruff check and format both files; report pass counts; then run `.venv/bin/python scripts/ringer/environment_narration/verifier_calibration.py --validate-corpus` (read-only, no --lock) and quote its output.
